wrong_answers_pool: Mitochondrial DNA undergoes rapid crossing over in Neanderthal populations
Non-African populations show vastly higher genetic diversity than indigenous African populations
Mitochondrial DNA is identical to Y-chromosome DNA in all human populations
mtDNA does not mutate and has remained 100% frozen since the origin of life
Mitochondrial DNA can only be extracted from hominin teeth fossils
African populations possess zero mutations in their mitochondrial genome
explanation: mtDNA is inherited strictly maternally without recombination, and molecular clock dating confirms all modern humans descend from an African maternal population ~150,000-200,000 ya.

question: In a diagnostic symposium at Academic Medical Centre in Durban, Dr. Chloe highlights the clinical finding: Which hominin was the first to use fire, manufacture Acheulean teardrop handaxes, and be the first hominin species to migrate out of Africa into Europe and Asia?
correct_answer: Homo erectus ('Turkana Boy')
wrong_answers_pool: Homo habilis ('Handy Man')
Australopithecus afarensis ('Lucy')
Australopithecus africanus
Homo naledi
Ardipithecus ramidus
Paranthropus boisei
explanation: Homo erectus exhibited a larger brain (~900-1100 cm3), perfected Acheulean stone tools, mastered fire, and successfully migrated across Eurasia.

question: During clinical rounds led by Dr. Jaco at Pathology Laboratory in Pretoria, trainees assess: Why does the observation that modern indigenous African populations possess the greatest genetic diversity of any human population on Earth support the 'Out of Africa' hypothesis?
correct_answer: African populations are the oldest extant human populations, having had the longest period of time to accumulate spontaneous genetic mutations and diversity
wrong_answers_pool: African populations have the highest mutation rates due to intense solar radiation
African populations interbred with dinosaurs during the Pleistocene
Non-African populations are ancient and have lost all genetic diversity through disease
Africans were the last group to evolve, so they contain all combined traits
Genetic diversity only accumulates in tropical rainforest biomes
It proves that humans evolved simultaneously on all six continents
explanation: Older populations accumulate greater numbers of neutral mutations over time; migrating populations carried only a subset of alleles (founder effect).

question: In a medical audit conducted by Dr. Anke at Regional Clinic in East London, the clinical team evaluates: Which famous fossil hominin skull was discovered in 1924 by Raymond Dart at Taung in South Africa, representing the first recognized specimen of Australopithecus africanus?
correct_answer: The Taung Child
wrong_answers_pool: Mrs Ples (StW 53)
Little Foot (StW 573)
Karabo
Lucy (AL 288-1)
Turkana Boy (WT 15000)
Handy Man (OH 7)
Cradle Man
explanation: Raymond Dart identified the fossilized skull and endocranial cast of a juvenile hominin at Taung, naming it Australopithecus africanus.

question: In a diagnostic symposium at University Teaching Hospital in Mbombela, Dr. Nandi highlights the clinical finding: Which hominin species, discovered in the Rising Star cave system by Lee Berger's team in 2013, possessed a small brain (~500 cm3) yet human-like hands and feet, with evidence suggesting intentional body disposal?
correct_answer: Homo naledi
wrong_answers_pool: Homo habilis
Homo erectus
Australopithecus afarensis
Homo neanderthalensis
Australopithecus africanus
Homo floresiensis
explanation: Homo naledi was discovered deep in the Dinaledi chamber, exhibiting a unique mosaic of primitive australopithecine-like and derived human-like anatomy.
